label: scenario
evidence: In commit b97bdbfb3304ef03a923bff1070e629d916919dc, LearningAutomation fingerprinted baseline conditions as {generation: baseline.generation, active: baseline.active} for experiment deduplication. Although baseline.generation is used for CAS adoption fencing, including it in deduplication caused store bookkeeping operations (such as store.recover('retire', ...)) or returning to an existing baseline to change the fingerprint and trigger redundant automatic background trials on unchanged inputs, violating the no-unchanged-automatic-retry criteria. The fix removed generation from the fingerprint, hashing only baseline.active.
cue: When computing deduplication fingerprints or cache keys for background trials or automated experiments against a state store that tracks optimistic concurrency using generation numbers
check: Does the deduplication fingerprint depend only on the semantic content of the evaluation inputs (such as the active baseline) rather than store generation or bookkeeping counters that mutate on recovery or administrative actions?
